Nine places to keep handy, each checked to load before being listed here.

- **FDA guidance: *Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures — Scope and Application*
  (2003)** — <https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/part-11-electronic-records-electronic-signatures-scope-and-application>.
  The guidance this module's predicate-rule definition, narrow-interpretation passage, and
  documentation recommendation all come from. Use it when you need the full context around any of
  those quotes, or when you want to read the legacy-system and copies-of-records sections ahead of
  next module.

- **FDA guidance: *Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers* (2018)** —
  <https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/data-integrity-and-compliance-drug-cgmp-questions-and-answers>.
  Source for the static/dynamic distinction (Question 1d) and the paper-printout-from-stand-alone-instrument
  answer (Question 10) this module quotes. Also where modules 1 and 2's ALCOA and audit-trail
  material came from, if you want one document covering all three.

- **Cornell Legal Information Institute (LII): 21 CFR § 11.2** —
  <https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.2>. A clean, citable, non-FDA rendering of the exact
  regulation quoted in full above — useful to hand a colleague who wants to read 11.2 on its own,
  outside this course's framing.

- **[Video 15 of 35 : FDA's 2003 Part 11 Guidance — Scope and Narrow
  Interpretation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nM8soKskDGo)** (Pharma Best Practices, from
  oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. An industry training channel's
  walkthrough of the 2003 scope guidance and its narrow interpretation; not FDA's own and not
  blood-specific, so use it as a second explanation and check anything it says against the
  guidance text quoted in the lesson. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR § 606.160, Records](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)** —
  the blood-establishment predicate rule this module names for DED-0458 and Fairview's donor file.
  Read the whole section, not just the paragraph a lesson quotes, to see every record type it
  requires Lakeshore to keep. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR § 606.100, Standard operating
  procedures](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)** — the second predicate rule named
  in the lesson, and the natural home for the SOP line Fairview was missing. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cornell LII: Title 21, Part 11 browse index](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/part-11)**
  — all of Part 11 in one place, so you can see § 11.2's neighbors (scope, definitions, controls,
  signatures) in context. Handy for seeing how little of Part 11 says anything about *which*
  records are required, which is the predicate rules' job. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Federal Register: Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures (the original Part 11 final
  rule)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/1997/03/20/97-6833/electronic-records-electronic-signatures)**
  — the rulemaking document that established Part 11, including FDA's own explanation of what the
  rule is for. Read it when you want the regulator's reasoning behind § 11.2's "in lieu of paper"
  framing, in FDA's words rather than a trainer's. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[UK MHRA: Guidance on GxP data integrity](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/guidance-on-gxp-data-integrity)**
  — a non-FDA regulator's data-integrity guidance, useful as a comparison read on how another
  authority treats records across formats. UK-regulated, so it does not govern Lakeshore; use it
  for perspective only, not as a citation for U.S. requirements. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about hybrid paper and electronic record systems.

- **[Data Integrity Focus, Part III: What Is the Problem with Hybrid Systems?](https://www.chromatographyonline.com/view/data-integrity-focus-part-iii-what-problem-hybrid-systems)** (LCGC International) — A practitioner article on why mixing paper and electronic records is risky and how the two sets of records drift apart. Written from the laboratory perspective but the reasoning carries to any hybrid workflow. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200). Page title checked.
- **[The Challenges of Ensuring Laboratory Data Integrity](https://www.gmp-compliance.org/gmp-news/the-challenges-of-ensuring-laboratory-data-integrity)** (ECA Academy) — Includes the problem of keeping paper and electronic records synchronized so they tell the same story. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200). Page title checked.
- **[GAMP Guide: Records & Data Integrity](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-records-pharmaceutical-data-integrity)** (ISPE) — Catalog page for a paid guide that includes material on hybrid records; useful to see how industry practitioners frame the topic. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200). Page title checked.
